column5: Question
column12: Explanation

column5: Within how long must you report an address change?
column12: A driver must report an address change to the MVC within one week, including when moving out of New Jersey.

column5: How many primary documents are required for identity verification?
column12: Standard applicants must provide at least one primary and one secondary identity document, totaling at least six ID points.

column5: Where must GDL decals be displayed?
column6: Top left corner of the front license plate
column7: Top right corner of the rear license plate
column8: Top left corner of front and rear license plates
column9: Top right corner of front and rear license plates
column11: Top left corner of front and rear license plates
column12: Drivers under 21 using a GDL permit or probationary license display a reflective decal on the top-left corner of each license plate.

column5: How many questions are on the knowledge test?
column12: The NJ knowledge test has 50 questions, in addition to an organ-donation survey question.

column5: What vision is required for a basic license applicant?
column12: A basic license applicant needs 20/50 vision with or without corrective lenses, with additional conditions for one-eyed vision.

column5: What is the required score on the knowledge test?
column12: A passing knowledge-test score is 80 percent: 40 correct answers out of 50 questions.

column5: According to the NJ manual's safety advice, children of what age or younger should ride in the back seat?
column12: The manual advises that children age 12 and younger ride in the back seat. This is a safety recommendation, not a minimum legal front-seat age.

column5: Who must wear a seatbelt?
column7: Passengers under the age of 18 and the driver
column8: All front seat passengers and passengers under the age of 18
column12: Everyone in the vehicle should be buckled up. New Jersey has seat-belt requirements for all seating positions.

column5: Which of these symptom groups may indicate carbon monoxide poisoning inside a vehicle?
column7: You see a thick, gray gas
column8: You experience headache, dizziness, loss of consciousness, nausea/vomiting, chest pain, or confusion
column11: You experience headache, dizziness, loss of consciousness, nausea/vomiting, chest pain, or confusion
column12: CO is odorless and colorless; possible symptoms include headache, dizziness, nausea, confusion, chest pain, and loss of consciousness. It can be fatal before symptoms appear.

column5: What is the speed limit on non-posted rural roadways?
column12: Unless otherwise posted, the listed speed limit on rural roadways with no posted limit is 50 mph.

column5: In which scenario is passing permitted?
column7: One center line is broken on your side
column8: One center line is broken, but it is on the opposite side
column9: Both center lines are broken, but you are within 50 feet of an intersection
column11: One center line is broken on your side
column12: A center line broken on your side permits passing when otherwise safe and legal; solid lines on your side prohibit passing.

column5: On a two-lane road, how far must you stop from a school bus displaying flashing red lights?
column12: On a two-lane road with a school bus displaying flashing red lights, stop at least 25 feet away.

column5: What is the car length rule for following distance?
column6: One car length back per 10 mph
column7: Two car lengths back per 10 mph
column8: One car length back per 20 mph
column11: One car length back per 10 mph
column12: A common following-distance rule is about one car length (20 feet) for every 10 mph. The three-second-plus rule is another method.

column5: What is the minimum time gap recommended by the three-seconds-plus following-distance rule?
column12: The three-seconds-plus rule requires at least three seconds between your car and the vehicle ahead at a fixed roadside marker.

column5: At approximately what speed can hydroplaning begin on a wet road?
column12: The manual says hydroplaning can begin at about 35 mph, with risk increasing as speed increases.

column5: Which one of these is a factor that determines blood alcohol concentration?
column12: The four BAC factors listed in the manual are amount consumed, body weight, speed of drinking, and food eaten.

column5: For drivers age 21 or older, what BAC is at or above New Jersey's statutory DUI threshold?
column12: A BAC of 0.08 percent or higher violates the adult BAC limit; impairment can make driving illegal even below that level.

column5: What does it mean to be a good host in terms of alcohol according to the driver’s manual?
column6: Serving the best quality alcohol to your guests
column7: Making sure to offer everyone a drink
column8: Helping your friends into their car, so they can drive home, since they are drunk
column9: Not letting someone drive themself home if they are drunk
column11: Not letting someone drive themself home if they are drunk
column12: A responsible host should not let an intoxicated guest drive and should arrange safe transportation or a place to stay.

column5: What is implied consent law?
column6: You are required to let officers search your vehicle when you are pulled over
column7: You are required to submit to a breath test, following an arrest for intoxication, from an officer or hospital staff with penalties given if you refuse
column8: You do not have to submit to a breath test, following an arrest for intoxication, from an officer or hospital staff
column9: You are required to let officers change your engine if it does not work
column11: You are required to submit to a breath test, following an arrest for intoxication, from an officer or hospital staff with penalties given if you refuse
column12: On NJ roadways, motorists consent to an authorized breath test after an intoxicated-driving arrest. Refusal can lead to serious penalties.

column5: Up to how many points may be deducted after a full year with no violation or suspension and driving privileges in good standing?
column12: Up to three points may be deducted after a full violation-free, suspension-free year in good standing; the balance cannot go below zero.

column5: A driver that accumulates 6+ points in 3 years is subject to …
column6: A surcharge of $150 for the 6 points plus $25 for every additional point
column11: A surcharge of $150 for the 6 points plus $25 for every additional point
column12: Six points posted within three years cause a $150 surcharge, plus $25 for each additional point.

column5: In most cases at intersections, which road user has priority while crossing the roadway?
column12: In most cases pedestrians have priority at intersections, including unmarked crosswalks. Drivers must obey applicable signals and controls.

column5: Why should you always leave plenty of room for motorcycles on the road?
column6: They need more room to turn
column7: They need more room to release exhaust
column8: They need more room to speed up
column9: They have shorter stopping distances than cars
column11: They have shorter stopping distances than cars
column12: The manual warns that motorcycles may brake in a shorter distance than other vehicles, so do not follow closely.

column5: What are blind spots?
column6: Areas where the driver cannot see you
column7: Areas where you cannot see the driver
column8: Designated areas where blind people can drive
column9: Designated areas where everyone on the road can see you
column11: Areas where the driver cannot see you
column12: A truck's No-Zones are areas its driver cannot see clearly, including major blind spots at the sides, front, and rear.

column5: What is the maximum fine for a license-plate cover that obscures lettering?
column12: Covers or holders that hide any letters on a license plate can lead to a fine of up to $100.

column5: How often must a qualifying gasoline-fueled NJ passenger vehicle, model year 1996 or newer and more than five model years old, pass inspection?
column12: Qualifying gasoline passenger vehicles more than five model years old, model year 1996 or newer, need inspection every two years.

column5: According to the NJ Driver Manual, what must be shown on the title of a vehicle classified under the Lemon Law?
column12: The manual specifically says a vehicle classified under the Lemon Law must have that classification shown on the title.

column5: What are warning signs?
column6: Guide motorists to a destination by clearly identifying the route
column7: Warn motorists of hazards and dangers ahead that are difficult to see
column11: Warn motorists of hazards and dangers ahead that are difficult to see
column12: Warning signs alert motorists to roadway hazards or conditions that require caution.

column5: What are guidance signs?
column6: Guide motorists to a destination by clearly identifying the route
column7: Warn motorists of hazards and dangers ahead that are difficult to see
column11: Guide motorists to a destination by clearly identifying the route
column12: Guidance signs identify destinations and routes so drivers can navigate toward them.

column5: What do orange, diamond-shaped traffic signs generally warn about?
column12: Orange diamond-shaped signs identify road construction and maintenance warnings, including detours and lane changes.
